history: ATR was founded in November 1981 as a 50/50 joint venture (GIE) between Aérospatiale of France (now Airbus) and Aeritalia of Italy (now Leonardo). Based in Toulouse, it is the world leader in regional turboprops with the ATR 42 and ATR 72 families, selling more than 1,700 aircraft to some 200 operators in nearly 100 countries. Nathalie Tarnaud Laude is CEO through 31 October 2026, when Vittorio Lorenzo Della Bella takes over.
key_people: Nathalie Tarnaud Laude (CEO to 31 Oct 2026); Vittorio Lorenzo Della Bella (CEO from 1 Nov 2026); Patrick Bergues (CFO from 1 Nov 2026)
specialties: ATR 42-600; ATR 72-600; ATR 72-600F freighter; regional turboprops
notable_clients: Some 200 operators in nearly 100 countries (company-published); individual order customers not enumerated
ownership: 50/50 joint venture of Airbus and Leonardo
notes: CEO transition announced September 2026. Fuselage/tail built by Leonardo in Italy; final assembly, flight test and delivery in Toulouse.

history: Airbus was created in 1970 as a European consortium (Airbus Industrie GIE) and became a single integrated company, EADS, in 2000; the group was renamed Airbus Group in 2014 and Airbus SE in 2017. It is the world's largest commercial planemaker by deliveries, producing the A220, A320neo, A330neo and A350 families. As of June 2026 it held a backlog of 9,222 commercial aircraft.
key_people: Guillaume Faury (CEO); Amparo Moraleda (Chair, from 1 Oct 2026)
specialties: A220; A320neo family; A330neo; A350 family (incl. A350F freighter); commercial aircraft
notable_clients: Air China and Shenzhen Airlines (55 aircraft: 15 A350-900, 40 A320neo, disclosed Jul 2026); Hainan Airlines (40 A320neo, disclosed Jul 2026); China Eastern Airlines; Turkish Airlines; Delta Air Lines; SMBC Aviation Capital; Atlas Air (A350F); FLYONE Armenia (2 A321neo, airline's first direct Airbus purchase, disclosed Sep 2026); Biman Bangladesh (4 A350-900 + 6 A321neo, firm order signed Oct 7, 2026); Avolon (110 aircraft: 75 A320neo + 35 A330neo, firm with options for 100 more, announced Oct 9, 2026; subject to Bohai Leasing shareholder approval expected before end of Oct 2026); Aviation Capital Group (75 A320neo family aircraft, firm order announced Oct 16, 2026 — largest order in ACG's history; deliveries 2032–2035); Air Cairo (15 A320neo, firm order signed Sep 8, 2026 at the El Alamein International Airshow — airline's first direct Airbus purchase; CFM LEAP-1A engines)
ownership: Publicly listed (Euronext Paris, Frankfurt, Spanish exchanges); France 10.9%, Germany 10.8%, Spain 4.1%
notes: Operational HQ Blagnac, France; legal seat Leiden, Netherlands. Phone/email shown are Airbus Media Relations as published in Airbus press releases; no general HQ switchboard is published. A350F freighter completed its maiden flight (four hours, MSN700 F-WXLD) from Toulouse on 29 Sep 2026; certification campaign (~400 flight hours, two test aircraft) targets entry into service in H2 2027; ~115 firm orders reported by Sep 2026 (incl. Atlas Air 20; Air China Cargo, AviLease, Etihad and Starlux 10 each).

history: The Boeing Company was founded in 1916 by William Boeing in Seattle and grew into the world's largest aerospace company. Boeing Commercial Airplanes (BCA), headquartered in Renton, Washington, designs, assembles and markets the 737, 767, 777 and 787 families. Under group CEO Kelly Ortberg (from August 2024) the company is rebuilding production and quality after the 737 MAX crises and a 53-day 2024 machinist strike.

specialties: 737 family; 767; 777 family; 787 Dreamliner; freighter and business-jet variants
notable_clients: Turkish Airlines (100 737-8 + 50 options, finalised Sep 2026; up to 75 787 ordered 2025); Korean Air (103 aircraft incl. 777-9, 787-10, 737 MAX 10, 777-8F, signed Sep 2026); Ethiopian Airlines (8 777-8F + 2 777F, announced Oct 2026, first African 777-8F customer); Biman Bangladesh (5 787-10 + 6 737-8 signed ~Oct 2026; 25 Boeing commitments total); Avolon (140 737 MAX, firm order announced Oct 9, 2026; subject to Bohai Leasing shareholder approval expected before end of Oct 2026)
ownership: Division of The Boeing Company (publicly listed, NYSE)

Definitive agreement signed Aug 2026 to sell Wisk Aero, Insitu and SkyGrid subsidiaries to Archer Aviation (all-stock; Boeing to hold ~16.5% Archer stake plus technology-sharing arrangement); HSR waiting period expired 18 Sep 2026; closing expected by end of 2026 subject to remaining approvals.

history: Founded in 1942 in Valcourt, Quebec by Joseph-Armand Bombardier as a snowmobile maker, Bombardier grew into a global transport conglomerate. After divesting rail and commercial aircraft programmes (C Series to Airbus, CRJ to Mitsubishi, Dash 8 to De Havilland, 2019-2020), it is now a pure-play business-jet company. Led by president and CEO Éric Martel, it builds the Challenger and Global families near Montreal.
key_people: Éric Martel (President & CEO); Pierre Beaudoin (Chairman)
specialties: Global 7500/6500/6000; Challenger 650/350; Bombardier Defense special-mission aircraft
notable_clients: Multinational corporations, charter/fractional providers, governments and private individuals (company-published categories); individual customers not disclosed
notes: Learjet production ended 2022. Fleet of ~5,000 aircraft in service; global service network.

history: The Commercial Aircraft Corporation of China was established on 11 May 2008 in Shanghai as a state-owned builder of large passenger aircraft. Its ARJ21 regional jet (now C909) was followed by the C919 narrowbody, which first flew in 2017 and entered commercial service in 2023. The C929 widebody is under development and the company is pursuing international certification.
key_people: He Dongfeng (Chairman); Zhao Yuerang (President)
specialties: C909 (ARJ21) regional jet; C919 narrowbody; C929 widebody (in development); C939/C949 studies
notable_clients: China Eastern Airlines (launch C919 operator); Air China (first international C919 commercial flight, Aug 2026); China Southern Airlines
notes: C919 order book passed 1,061 aircraft in 2023. EU/US certification pursued; EU validation expected 2025 per industry reports.

history: Founded in 1984 in Baraboo, Wisconsin by brothers Alan and Dale Klapmeier, Cirrus moved to Duluth, Minnesota in 1994. Its SR series, with the CAPS whole-airframe parachute as standard, became the world's best-selling piston aircraft, followed by the Vision Jet, the first single-engine personal jet. Acquired by China's CAIGA in 2011, it listed in Hong Kong in 2024; Zean Nielsen has been CEO since 2019.

specialties: SR Series piston aircraft (SR20/SR22/SR22T); Vision Jet single-engine personal jet
notable_clients: Private owners and flight-training operators; individual customers not disclosed

notes: World's largest producer of piston-powered aircraft since 2013.

history: CubCrafters was founded in 1980 in Yakima, Washington by Jim Richmond, evolving the classic Piper Super Cub into modern backcountry aircraft. It designs and manufactures Experimental, LSA and Part 23 certified aircraft, including the Carbon Cub family and the XCub. Under president and CEO Patrick Horgan, it is developing the turbine-powered Carbon Cub ULT, with deliveries expected in 2027.
key_people: Patrick Horgan (President & CEO); Brad Damm (Vice President)
specialties: Carbon Cub SS/EX/FX; XCub; NXCub; Top Cub; Carbon Cub ULT (in development); builder-assist programme

history: Daher was founded in 1863 in Marseille as a maritime and foundry business, bought by the Daher family 35 years later. It entered aircraft manufacturing by acquiring Socata (2008-2014) and Quest Aircraft (2019), maker of the Kodiak. The family-owned group now builds the TBM turboprop family in Tarbes, France and the Kodiak in Sandpoint, Idaho, alongside aerostructures and logistics businesses.
key_people: Didier Kayat (CEO); Patrick Daher (Chairman)
specialties: TBM 910/960/980 single-engine turboprops; Kodiak 100/900 utility turboprops; aerostructures for Airbus, Dassault, Embraer and Gulfstream
notable_clients: Private owners and utility operators; aerostructures supplied to Airbus, Dassault, Embraer and Gulfstream (company-published)
notes: TBM 980 launched 2026 with Garmin G3000 PRIME avionics. Group revenue EUR 1.9bn (2025); 14,500 employees.

history: Founded by Marcel Bloch in 1929 (Société des Avions Marcel Bloch), Dassault Aviation became France's premier combat-aircraft maker with the Mirage and Rafale, and a leader in business jets with the Falcon family. It has delivered over 10,000 aircraft to 90 countries, with 2,100 Falcons in service. Chairman and CEO Éric Trappier was renewed in 2026; the Falcon 10X is in development.
key_people: Éric Trappier (Chairman & CEO)
specialties: Falcon family of business jets (Falcon 10X in development); Rafale multirole fighter; special-mission Falcons

Dassault Group led since 2025 by Éric Trappier.; Falcon 10X: second test aircraft (SN2) joined the flight-test fleet (reported Oct 5, 2026); certification and entry into service moved to 2029 (was 2027) — ~2.5-year certification campaign expected per Trappier.

history: De Havilland Aircraft of Canada traces its heritage to 1928 and the legendary Beaver, Twin Otter and Dash 8. The modern company was reconstituted in 2019 when Longview Aviation Capital acquired the Dash 8 programme from Bombardier, uniting the full product line; Viking Air, Longview and Pacific Sky Training were consolidated under the De Havilland brand in February 2022. Led by CEO Brian Chafe, the 100% Canadian-owned company builds the DHC-6 Twin Otter, Dash 8 and the DHC-515 Firefighter.
key_people: Brian Chafe (CEO)
specialties: DHC-6 Twin Otter; DHC-8 Dash 8; DHC-515 Firefighter; support for 3,000+ aircraft in service
notable_clients: Twin Otter and Dash 8 operators worldwide (3,000+ aircraft in service); individual customers not enumerated
notes: Viking Air consolidated under the De Havilland brand in 2022 (no separate row). De Havilland Field (Alberta) groundbreaking May 2026. Heritage 1928; modern company reconstituted 2019. Dash 8-400 recertified to ICAO Chapter 14 noise standards (Oct 2026), the first regional aircraft so recertified.

history: Founded in 1981 as Hoffmann Flugzeugbau in Friesach, Austria, the company became Diamond Aircraft Industries in the 1990s. Known for composite piston singles and twins - the DA20, DA40, DA42 and seven-seat DA62 - it is a leading supplier to flight-training fleets worldwide. Acquired by China's Wanfeng Aviation in December 2017, it is headquartered in Wiener Neustadt with production in Austria, Canada and China.
key_people: Bin Chen (Chairman); Frank Zhang (CEO, Austria division)
specialties: DA20; DA40 NG; DA42-VI; DA62; DA50 RG piston aircraft; flight-training simulators; Austro Engine piston engines
notable_clients: Private pilots, flight-training operators and institutions worldwide (5,500+ aircraft); individual customers not disclosed
notes: D-Jet very light jet programme discontinued 2013.

history: Embraer was created by the Brazilian government on 19 August 1969 (Decree-Law 770) in São José dos Campos and privatized in 1994. It became the world's third-largest commercial planemaker with the ERJ and E-Jet regional jet families, and later built a leading executive-jet business with the Phenom and Praetor families. It is publicly listed; Francisco Gomes Neto is president and CEO.
key_people: Francisco Gomes Neto (President & CEO); Arjan Meijer (CEO, Commercial Aviation)
specialties: E-Jets E2 family (E190-E2, E195-E2); E-Jets; Phenom and Praetor executive jets; C-390 Millennium military airlifter
notable_clients: Porter Airlines (largest E2 customer); Azul; Binter Canarias; Luxair; KLM Cityhopper; LATAM Airlines; SAS; Avelo Airlines; Abra Group (Avianca/GOL, 20 E195-E2, Jul 2026); Fuji Dream Airlines; Azorra (+15 E2s, announced Oct 8, 2026, fourth increase to Dec 2021 order); ANA Holdings (23 E190-E2 firm + 5 options — agreement for eight additional E190-E2s signed Sep 3, 2026, expanding the Feb 2025 order; deliveries from 2028); Japan Airlines (16 firm + 10 options E190-E2 for J-AIR, announced Oct 14, 2026; deliveries from FY2029, replacing the E170/E190 fleet)

Mahindra Group & Embraer identified Nagpur for a potential C-390 Millennium final assembly line (announced Oct 1, 2026); preparatory industrial-planning discussions, conditional on India selecting the C-390 under the IAF MTA programme.; First E175 with new-generation RECARO seats delivered to American Airlines (Oct 19, 2026).

history: Gulfstream was founded in 1958 and became the benchmark brand in large-cabin business jets. A General Dynamics company headquartered in Savannah, Georgia, it has delivered more than 2,800 aircraft. The current line-up spans the G300 to the flagship G700 and G800 ultra-long-range jets, led by president Mark Burns since 2015.
key_people: Mark Burns (President); Phebe Novakovic (Chairman & CEO, General Dynamics)
specialties: G700 and G800 ultra-long-range jets; G600; G500; G400; G300; large-cabin business jets
notable_clients: Private, corporate and government customers; individual customer identities not published

history: Honda Aircraft Company was established in August 2006 as a wholly owned subsidiary of Honda Motor to commercialize the HondaJet, whose over-wing engine-mount design originated in Honda R&D. Based in Greensboro, North Carolina, it delivered its first customer aircraft in late 2015 and has delivered more than 275 HondaJets. The HondaJet Elite II is in production and the larger HondaJet Echelon is in development, under president and CEO Hideto Yamasaki.
key_people: Hideto Yamasaki (President & CEO)
specialties: HondaJet Elite II very light jet; HondaJet Echelon (in development)
notable_clients: Owner-pilots, corporate operators and air-taxi companies (company-published categories); individual customers not disclosed
ownership: Wholly owned subsidiary of Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (publicly listed)
notes: Celebrated 20 years in August 2026. ~1,000 associates on a 133-acre campus at Piedmont Triad International Airport.

history: Pilatus was founded on 16 December 1939 in Stans, Switzerland, initially to service Swiss Air Force aircraft. It built its name on STOL and trainer aircraft - the PC-6 Porter, PC-7, PC-9 and PC-21 - and entered business aviation with the PC-12 (1994) and the PC-24 jet. Led by CEO Markus Bucher since 2013, it remains Swiss-owned and independent.
key_people: Markus Bucher (CEO); Hansueli Loosli (Chairman)
specialties: PC-12 NGX single-engine turboprop; PC-24 twinjet (STOL-capable); PC-7 MKX and PC-21 trainers
notable_clients: Government/military trainer operators and private owners; individual customers not disclosed
notes: Phone as published in an official Pilatus press release (may be a press/media line). Subsidiaries in the USA (Broomfield, Colorado) and Australia. Garmin Emergency Autoland certified on the PC-12 PRO by FAA and EASA (announced Sep 2026).

history: Founded in 1927 as the Taylor Brothers Aircraft Manufacturing Company, Piper became one of general aviation's 'Big Three' with the J-3 Cub and PA-28 Cherokee. Based in Vero Beach, Florida, it was acquired in 2009 by the Government of Brunei (via Imprimis). Under president and CEO John Calcagno since 2021, it builds the M-Class, Archer, Seminole and trainer lines, posting record recent sales of 291 aircraft in both 2024 and 2025.
key_people: John Calcagno (President & CEO)

notes: Phone as published in the official 2026 Piper trainer brochure footer. ~1,500 employees; ~144,000 aircraft built since 1927.

history: Tecnam's heritage dates to 1948, when the Pascale brothers began designing light aircraft in Italy; the present company was established in Capua in March 1986. It is one of the world's largest producers of piston training and general-aviation aircraft, including the P2002, P2006T twin and P2012 Traveller. The family-run company, led by managing director Giovanni Pascale Langer, celebrated its 30th anniversary in 2016.

Phone/email as published in official Tecnam releases.; Third-generation succession effective Oct 8, 2026: Giovanni Pascale Langer (Managing Director since 2019) appointed CEO; Paolo Pascale Langer became President (announced Oct 14, 2026).

history: Textron Aviation was formed in March 2014 when Textron combined Cessna with newly acquired Beechcraft (Beech Holdings, US$1.4bn). The Wichita-based unit sells the Beechcraft, Cessna and Hawker brands and, since 2022, Pipistrel light aircraft; the standalone eAviation reporting division was ended in January 2026. Brian Rohloff became president and CEO on 31 August 2026, succeeding Ron Draper.

notes: Pipistrel included in Textron Aviation scope (no separate row); eAviation absorbed January 2026. 250,000+ aircraft delivered across brands; customers in 170+ countries.

history: Founded on 28 March 1932 as the Irkutsk Aviation Plant, the company became Irkut Corporation in 2002 and UAC's civil-airliner division, absorbing Sukhoi Civil Aircraft in 2018. In August 2023 it rebranded as Yakovlev, with the Sukhoi Superjet 100 redesignated the SJ-100 and the MC-21 under the Yakovlev name. Import-substituted MC-21 and SJ-100 certification and serial deliveries have been delayed, with MC-21 introduction now expected in 2027.

history: Formed in 1992 as Eurocopter from the helicopter divisions of France's Aerospatiale and Germany's MBB, uniting decades of rotary-wing heritage. It became Airbus Helicopters in January 2014 after a rebranding of the Airbus Group. It is the world's largest civil helicopter manufacturer by deliveries, with assembly lines in Marignane, Donauworth and elsewhere.

Dublin lessor GD Helicopter Finance signed EUR 125m+ in financing (Oct 2026) to fund factory-new H160 and H175 helicopters in 2026-2027 (first H160 financed Sep 2026).

history: Founded in 1935 by Lawrence Dale Bell as Bell Aircraft Corporation in Buffalo, New York. It produced the Bell 47, the first helicopter certified for commercial use, in 1946. The helicopter business became Bell Helicopter and was acquired by Textron in 1960, forming today's Bell segment.
key_people: Danny Maldonado, President & CEO, Bell segment (effective Jan 4, 2026; per Textron press release of Oct 28, 2025)
specialties: 505 Jet Ranger X; 407; 429; 412; 525 Relentless (in development); V-22 Osprey (military, with Boeing); MV-75/FLRAA tiltrotor (military)

MV-75 (FLRAA) tiltrotor: first airframe fuselage nearing completion at Wichita (reported Oct 2026), for nacelle/lift-surface integration at Amarillo.

history: Founded by Argentine inventor and helicopter pioneer Augusto Cicare (1937-2022), whose first helicopter, the CH-1, flew in 1958 - the first helicopter designed and built in South America. The family company in Saladillo, Buenos Aires province, produces a family of ultralight kit helicopters (CH-7B, CH-7T, CH-8, CH-12) and the SVH-4 training system, exporting to dozens of countries.

history: Composite-FX of Trenton, Florida, took over production of the Mosquito single-seat kit helicopter line in 2019 (from Innovator Technologies; originally Mosquito Aviation, designed by John Uptigrove, 2004). It sells the XE series as amateur-built kits and factory-finished aircraft, with over 400 kit deliveries reported.

history: Curti Aerospace is the aerospace division of Curti S.p.A., a family industrial group founded in 1955 and a long-time supplier of aeronautical alloy parts to companies including Leonardo. The Zefhir two-seat turbine ultralight program began in 2013 in partnership with PBS Velka Bites (engine) and Junkers Profly, partly funded by the European Commission; the first flight was in 2017.

It branched into helicopter design with new European microlight rules, and the H3 EasyFlyer (now H3 Sport) two-seat ultralight helicopter became its sole product in the mid-2010s.

notes: Phone and general email published on official pricelist. Also developing unmanned/aerial-solutions platforms.

history: Founded in 1959 by mining engineer Rudolph J. 'Rudy' Enstrom at the Menominee-Marinette Twin County Airport in Michigan. The piston F-28 was certified in 1965, followed by the 280 and the turbine 480. The company ceased operations and filed Chapter 7 bankruptcy in January 2022; Surack Enterprises bought the assets in May 2022 and restarted production, with a new FAA production certificate issued in 2023.

notable_clients: Training and law-enforcement operators worldwide (individual operators not aggregated in company disclosures)

history: Founded in 2000 in Aix-en-Provence, France, by Bruno Guimbal, a former Eurocopter engineer. The two-seat Cabri G2, first flown in 2005, was designed from scratch as a modern piston trainer with Fenestron tail rotor. The 400th Cabri G2 flew in January 2026, and the larger GrandCabri G5 was launched in March 2026.
key_people: Bruno Guimbal, Chairman and CEO (founder)

The HX50 was publicly launched in August 2020 and has accumulated around 1,200 pre-orders/deposits. The maiden flight was delayed by GT50 engine development and is now expected in 2027.

notes: Not yet certified; first flight now scheduled for 2027 per the company's FAQ (previously targeted late 2026). HX50 is initially to fly under experimental/permit-to-fly rules; full UK CAA type certification targeted for the HC50. Contact via hillhelicopters.com forms.

history: Founded in 1945 by Charles Kaman in Bloomfield, Connecticut, as the Kaman Aircraft Corporation, pioneering intermeshing-rotor (synchropter) helicopters. The K-MAX (K-1200) first flew in 1991 for external-load operations. Kaman was taken private by Arcline Investment Management in a USD 1.8bn deal completed April 2024.

history: Founded in 2002 in Amaro (Udine), Italy, by Sergio Bortoluz to develop both the TK-250 turboshaft engine and a line of carbon-fibre light helicopters. The two-seat K1-S19 is certified as an ultralight (600 kg) and holds approvals in Germany, Sweden and Finland; the four-seat K2 followed, and the amphibious K3 Anfibio is in development.

history: Created in 2016 when AgustaWestland was merged into Leonardo-Finmeccanica as its Helicopters Division, uniting Italy's Agusta (founded 1907) and the UK's Westland (1915) heritage. AgustaWestland itself had been formed in 2000 and fully acquired by Finmeccanica in 2004. The division is headquartered at Cascina Costa di Samarate, Italy.

history: The current company was formed in 1999 when MD Helicopter Holdings acquired Boeing's civil helicopter product lines, inheriting the Hughes Helicopters lineage (Hughes Aircraft, 1947; Hughes Helicopters, 1955). After a Chapter 11 bankruptcy, its assets were bought in 2022 by an investment consortium, which relaunched production in Mesa, Arizona.

history: Founded in 1973 in Torrance, California, by engineer Frank Robinson, who had previously worked on helicopter programs at Bell, Hughes and Kaman. The two-seat R22 entered production in 1979 and became the world's best-selling civil helicopter. The R44 and turbine R66 followed, and Robinson remains the highest-volume civil helicopter maker in the world.
key_people: David Smith, Chairman and CEO
notable_clients: Thousands of flight schools, tour operators and private owners worldwide; no single major fleet orders are disclosed by the company
notes: Contact only via robinsonheli.com forms. Family-founded independent maker; still led from Torrance.

history: The Russian Helicopters holding (Vertolety Rossii) was established in 2007 to consolidate Russia's helicopter industry, including the Kazan and Ulan-Ude plants and the Mil and Kamov design bureaus. It is part of the Rostec state corporation. Civil production is centered on the Mi-8/17 family, Ka-32 and Ansat at Kazan.

specialties: Mi-8/17 family (civil variants); Ka-32 (civil firefighting/utility); Ansat (import-substituted variant with VK-650V engine in certification); Mi-38

The company restarted production of the 300C, 300CBi and 333 in Fort Worth, Texas. In April 2026 it was announced for sale as a going concern (Starman Bros auction).
